idiom_name: jest.mock module replacement with jest.fn stand-ins (MSW for wire-level)
implementation_notes: With no interfaces at runtime the stand-in is whatever object the client imported: jest.mock('./priceService') replaces the module with generated mocks and jest.fn plus mockResolvedValue supply canned answers, while a hand-written __mocks__ module supplies stand-ins with real behaviour. Nothing checks that the fake still matches the real module, so the drift risk moves to the exports themselves. When the contract is HTTP, Mock Service Worker stands in for the service at the network layer and intercepts requests from any client library, which exercises the real client code, serialization and error handling against declared handlers - the preferred seam when the wire format matters.
pitfalls: jest.mock calls are hoisted above the imports, so a factory cannot close over variables defined in the file; use jest.requireActual for partial mocks or a __mocks__ module instead.
A module-level mock is invisible to the test reader: renaming or deleting an export leaves the fake intact and the test green while the production path is broken.
Stubbing the HTTP client object couples every test to that client; swapping fetch for axios silently bypasses the stub, which is the failure mode network-level interception exists to avoid.

variants.name: Hand-written manual mock module (__mocks__)
variants.implementation_notes: A manual mock next to the real module keeps canned data and small behaviours in one place that every test file shares, which is what jest means by writing a manual mock to override a module dependency. It is the readable option when the stand-in needs behaviour (lookup tables, invariants, scripted failures) rather than call recording.
pitfalls: A manual mock that drifts from the real module's exports fails only at runtime, deep inside a test that never mentioned the service.
Automatic and manual mocks interact: calling jest.mock without a factory still picks up __mocks__ entries, which surprises readers who expected the real module.

variants.name: MSW network-level handlers (service, not module, is replaced)
variants.implementation_notes: Mock Service Worker intercepts requests at the network level, so the same handler definitions work in the browser, in Node and for development and debugging, and they apply to every request library including the one you have not adopted yet. Handlers are declared as data (route plus response) rather than as code that mimics an interface, which is why the same definitions can serve tests and an offline development mode.
pitfalls: Handlers strip query parameters by design, so a test that intends to assert on the query string must read it from the request URL itself.
Concurrent tests that both mutate handler state must be scoped with the server boundary API, otherwise they interfere with each other.
Request clients that cache responses (react-query, SWR, Apollo) can serve stale data between tests unless their caches are cleared.
